direction.reason: RETAINED slight weakening after the weekend demand and geopolitical review. The completed ECB Q&A keeps conditional tightening active; Q3 growth and AI investment are real support, and the SPF shows inflation persistence. German underlying cooling, limited second-round pass-through, restrictive credit, French financing risk and energy-income damage still modestly dominate through the next domestic test. China's demand miss adds external opposition to growth without proving a European contraction. The already-anticipated December path is not new upside. A firmer multi-meeting ECB path or credible energy/credit relief defeats this balance. Against USD the equal negative grades are not a clean entry; GBP has stronger later-path support, and JPY the clearer current normalisation/haven case.

evidence.title: Later ECB sources qualify tightening with a post-December pause and financing drag
evidence.facts: Reuters observed October29 19:40UTC version reports meeting sources judged December17 hike all but certain, but expected a pause thereafter because market-based borrowing costs rose sharply. Report says ECB estimates circulated before meeting imply cumulative2027-28 growth drag100bp and inflation drag90bp versus September baseline. These are scenario/model estimates, not realised GDP/inflation or a publicly adopted commitment. DWS describes fewer hikes; Reuters survey majority sees one or two more, separately from earlier preview report-time money markets roughly three. Survey, source views and pricing are distinct horizons/providers and not a matched quantitative repricing calculation. Full ECB Q&A conditional further tightening remains valid; no new delivered rate action. This body was available before prior03:31UTC assessment but omitted from its weighting; present correction does not invent a later market reversal minute.

evidence.facts:
Official SPF headline forecasts 2026/27/28 = 3.0/2.6/2.0 vs 2.7/2.2/2.0; core 2.4/2.5/2.2, revisions 0/+0.2/+0.1; 2031 headline 2.0 anchored. SMA collected Oct12-14, 69 respondents, median DFR 2.50 Oct, 2.75 Dec flat through 2027Q4, 2.50 early2028, 2.25 late2028. This is survey vintage not postmeeting market pricing or ECB commitment. 64 company contacts Sept28-Oct7 report moderate Q3/Q4 growth, AI/electrification/defence strength but weak retail/process industries/construction; declining headcounts, productivity helps services.

Stronger Q3 selling prices with some Q4 moderation; ~90% consumer-facing firms report only partial/limited pass-through. Expected wages 3.0 in26/2.9 in27, 40% see higher wage demand risk vs20 but majority no notable effect. No claim Europe has no AI investment; sources explicitly show it. One coherent survey-stage review, not independent vote count.

evidence.title: Lane actual speech recognises European AI growth; annex retains financing and inflation constraints
evidence.facts: Lane says AI already contributes significantly to euro-area growth through adoption and global supply chains, while economywide productivity timing remains uncertain. Corporate contacts report AI adds about10% to planned capex this year; this is survey evidence, not realised aggregate investment. Tech-goods inflation has limited headline weight. AI firms are more sensitive to monetary tightening through financing needs and capital-market segmentation. European purchases of US technology assets in Q2 are dated portfolio data, not current October30 flow. Annex retains financing, credit, energy, wage and inflation context with original cutoffs; AI scenarios and a neutral-rate range are not forecasts or a new rate commitment. Speech explicitly does not review yesterday ECB meeting and expresses personal views. Resolves16:10UTC Lane stage; growth support is material opposition to mild EUR weakness, but supplies no fresh collective acceleration or evidence that credit/import-energy opposition has disappeared.

evidence.title: China factory PMI falls below expectations; services and construction also soften
evidence.facts: October official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 from 50.1, below the Reuters poll of 50.0. Non-manufacturing fell to 49.7 from 50.2. New orders, exports and production showed weakness. First months of quarters are typically softer, technology-related sectors remained stronger, and economists still expected the annual growth target to be met. The miss is fresh weekend demand information, not proof of a collapse or a new policy-stimulus announcement.

evidence.title: ECB full Q&A keeps further tightening active despite financing restraint
evidence.facts: Lagarde confirmed a hike was debated before a unanimous hold. Further tightening remains the conditional direction absent major contrary developments. Higher long-term financing costs offset part of the energy shock. Instruments remain available for disorderly transmission; no TPI activation was announced. Her February departure does not change the current mandate or establish a successor policy path.

evidence.title: ECB lending survey: tighter standards and weaker demand
evidence.facts: Official October 27 ECB survey reports Q3 net tightening of firm credit standards of 9% versus prior-round expectations of 5%, and firm loan demand -6% versus an expected +4%. These are bank survey balances, not credit volumes or realised GDP. The survey was conducted September 21 to October 6 and is dated background, not a new October 29 release.
